title: Band-9 Samples: When do you visit other places, do you take photos or buy postcards? [Why/Why not?]
passage_text: This post contains ideas and band-9 sample answers (audio included) for the Cambridge IELTS 11 Academic Speaking Part 1 Question 3 Test 3 question: “When do you visit other places, do you take photos or buy postcards? [Why/Why not?]” Sample 1: Taking Photos Female Male While I love the idea of collecting postcards, I find that they often end up tucked away in drawers or boxes, forgotten. Hence, I’ve started to capture my memories through photographs instead. This way, I can easily store them digitally and revisit them anytime I wish, solving the problem of physical clutter. Sample 2: Taking Photos Female Male In this digital age, I find myself inclined to take photos when I roam around new places, rather than buying postcards. The contrast is stark when you think about it – while postcards offer a fixed, unchangeable view, photos allow me to capture the essence of my journey in a more dynamic and flexible manner. With my smartphone, I can take hundreds of pictures, edit them to my liking, and share them with my friends online, making the entire experience much more interactive and personal. Sample 3: Taking Photos Female Male Photography is an art form to me, so I always carry my camera when I travel. Capturing the unique aspects of a place, the light, the colors, the textures, gives me a sense of fulfillment. Although postcards offer a ready-made image, they lack the personal touch and creativity that comes from capturing a scene through my own lens. Sample 4: Taking Photos Female Male While some might argue that buying postcards is a traditional and romantic aspect of travel, I find taking photographs a more cost-effective and practical solution. Cameras and smartphones are ubiquitous these days, and taking photos doesn’t cost anything beyond the initial investment in the device. On the other hand, postcards can add up in cost, especially in popular tourist destinations. Plus, there’s the additional expense of postage if you plan to mail them. So, for budget-conscious travelers like myself, taking photos is the way to go. Sample 5: Buying Postcards Female Male When I’m exploring different locales, I prefer to acquire postcards as opposed to capturing snapshots. The primary reason for this preference is the artistic value that postcards hold. They’re often designed by local artists who beautifully encapsulate the essence of the place, showcasing its unique features in a compact, tangible form. This artistic representation is something a camera can’t entirely capture. Sample 6: Buying Postcards Female Male When I traverse to new places, I find myself more inclined to purchase postcards rather than snap photographs. The primary cause for this is the tangibility that a postcard offers. Holding a postcard, feeling its texture, and seeing the image on it, triggers a more vivid recall of the experience. It’s a physical piece of the place that I can bring back home, making the memory more prevalent in my mind. Sample 7: Buying Postcards Female Male While I do appreciate the immediacy of digital photos, I find that procuring postcards during my journeys introduces an element of anticipation that’s missing in the instant gratification of taking my own pictures. Waiting to see the artful depiction of the sites I’ve visited adds an extra layer of excitement to my travel experience, which is something I deeply cherish. Sample 8: Buying Postcards Female Male I’ve been accumulating postcards from every corner I’ve visited since I was a teenager. It’s a tradition I started with my first solo trip, and it’s grown into something of a personal collection. It’s not just about remembering the places I’ve been, but also about appreciating the unique artistic interpretations of those places. Sample 9: Both Female Male I’m an avid traveler and when I explore different regions, I tend to take photographs and also purchase postcards. The rationale behind this is my desire to share my experiences. Photos let me narrate my travel stories in detail to my loved ones back home. Meanwhile, postcards serve as small tokens of the places I’ve visited, which are perfect for gifting. Sample 10: Both Female Male I absolutely adore both taking snapshots and collecting postcards when I travel. It’s interesting to consider the juxtaposition between the digital and the physical. Photos, which are often stored digitally these days, offer a high-resolution, customizable record of my adventures. Postcards, however, present a more tactile, traditional keepsake that I can physically display in my home.
